# Quiet source forks

These are complete crates.io source distributions, **not unmodified upstream
packages**. Their published names/versions are preserved for type compatibility;
the path dependencies in this probe are mandatory. `Cargo.toml.orig` and
`.cargo_vcs_info.json` are preserved upstream records, not active manifests.
No registry patch or global logger/level/subscriber modification is required.

| Package | Source archive | SHA-256 | Packaged VCS revision | License |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mssql-tds 0.3.0 | <https://static.crates.io/crates/mssql-tds/mssql-tds-0.3.0.crate> | `c7a53513324677e601ca5b91e477840329ec6c244875fd55b155e5a8e8af7805` | `6541c6bacb9a59a322cb3e20801d3adb1b9e0970`, path `mssql-tds` | MIT |
| native-tls 0.2.18 | <https://static.crates.io/crates/native-tls/native-tls-0.2.18.crate> | `465500e14ea162429d264d44189adc38b199b62b1c21eea9f69e4b73cb03bbf2` | `3cf1877ee86814168255db6d73fbefc127211c1c` | MIT / Apache-2.0 |
| tokio-native-tls 0.3.1 | <https://static.crates.io/crates/tokio-native-tls/tokio-native-tls-0.3.1.crate> | `bbae76ab933c85776efabc971569dd6119c580d8f5d448769dec1764bf796ef2` | `775b6d69f42f76227c5a3c5ac5058da9ff095ca0`, path `tokio-native-tls` | MIT |

Copyright notices and packaged `LICENSE*` files are retained in each directory.
The archives can be retrieved with `curl --fail --location` from the URLs above;
the generator refuses an archive whose SHA does not match.
The generator also removes `tokio-native-tls`'s Apple-only `security-framework`
dev dependency: this vendored crate is used as a dependency, not as a workspace
test target, and that yanked `0.2` range otherwise blocks resolution of the
Linux workspace.

## Reproduction

From the probe directory, with those three archives in `$archives`:

```sh
python3 tools/vendor-quiet.py "$archives" /tmp/opencode/reproduced-quiet
diff -ru vendor/mssql-tds-0.3.0 /tmp/opencode/reproduced-quiet/vendor/mssql-tds-0.3.0
diff -ru vendor/native-tls-0.2.18 /tmp/opencode/reproduced-quiet/vendor/native-tls-0.2.18
diff -ru vendor/tokio-native-tls-0.3.1 /tmp/opencode/reproduced-quiet/vendor/tokio-native-tls-0.3.1
cargo test --locked --test vendor_guard
```

Use a fresh output directory. The generator never overwrites an existing fork.
It runs rustfmt from the repository-pinned Rust toolchain, using the repository
`rustfmt.toml` and each crate's edition, on every packaged Rust file. It visits
files individually with `skip_children=true` so cfg-specific and standalone
modules are covered without resolving a standalone module as a crate root.
Rustup and the pinned rustfmt component must be installed. A toolchain or
format configuration update may change the generated bytes and requires
regeneration, review, and an explicit inventory refresh.
`tools/seal-vendor.py` is an explicit review operation to refresh the inventory
after a reviewed update; it inventories the crate manifest plus all files under
the three vendor directories, not a crate-local or workspace `Cargo.lock`.
It must **not** be run automatically before tests.
`python3 tools/test-seal-vendor.py` runs the sealer twice in a disposable copy, verifies
the hashes are stable/correct, and confirms the checked-in inventory is
untouched.
The guard checks every packaged file (including manifests/build scripts), detects
additions/removals, pins the crate manifest, parses all Rust files without
target/cfg filtering, and rejects diagnostic invocations and instrumentation.
The crate uses the enclosing workspace lockfile; CI separately checks that its
normal dependency tree contains no SQLx.
Mutation controls prove that the syntax tripwire rejects qualified macros,
unqualified macros, spans, attributes, and diagnostic aliases.

## Deliberately narrow delta

`tools/vendor-quiet.py` is the entire transformation:

* Replace all 337 TDS `trace/debug/info/warn/error/event!` invocations, including
  fully qualified calls, with `quiet!`. This includes auth, DNS, endpoints,
  routing, TLS, raw packet dumps, errors, SQL, and platform-specific/spawned paths.
* Remove all 41 TDS `#[instrument(...)]` attributes and diagnostic macro imports.
* Apply the same operation to native-tls's four certificate-loading diagnostics.
* Define `quiet!` as a token-tree consumer expanding to an empty block: arguments
  are neither expanded, type-checked, formatted, nor evaluated. The retained
  argument text makes the original diagnostic sites reviewable. A `test-util`
  regression probe passes `panic!()` as an argument and must return normally.
* Remove active logging dependencies; wire both direct native-tls and its Tokio
  wrapper to the same local quiet native-tls fork. The wrapper's transport logic
  is unchanged. Remove its unused, yanked Apple-only test dependency so Cargo
  resolves the vendored library in this Linux workspace.
* Drop Cargo's ignored package-level resolver and duplicate license-file
  metadata on `mssql-tds`, and narrowly allow the two existing
  `unnecessary_lazy_evaluations` findings in `native-tls`. These manifest-only
  changes avoid manifest warnings and keep strict lints meaningful for the
  adapter itself.
* Retain upstream log-only locals/imports and explicitly allow only the unused
  warnings that their removal introduces. No protocol/control-flow refactor or
  general Clippy suppression is mixed into the security delta.
* Apply the pinned repository rustfmt configuration to all packaged Rust
  sources after the quiet transformation. This is a formatting-only step;
  it does not replace the independent syntax guard or review of regenerated
  source and inventory.

The generator is mechanical, not a general-purpose Rust rewriter. The complete
tree must still compile and pass the independent syntax/inventory guard after
any upstream update. Do not infer that a regex would handle a new release.
